requirement_text.REQ-044: Port the core value types and top-level dispatch of src/engine/transition.zig's transition() (per src/design/engine.md "Section EE-02: Pure Transition Function", L442) as a pure Letflow module -- no Ecto.Repo call, no I/O of any kind, no clock read, matching transition.zig's own header contract ("All state is passed in; all output is returned. No DB, no network, no clock") and the same purity bar REQ-028 already established for the graph validator. This requirement builds the SKELETON and its non-gateway node transitions only. The gateway bodies are separate requirements (REQ-050 exclusive, REQ-051 parallel split/join) that plug into the dispatch this requirement defines. Determinism is load-bearing: identical inputs always produce identical outputs. An unknown event type returns an error state, never raises. A token sitting on a node id absent from the snapshot graph returns an error state naming the inconsistency. HUMAN_TASK appends to pending_task_nodes; END moves the instance toward COMPLETED. Reuses REQ-028's DefinitionGraph/GraphNode/GraphEdge/NodeType structs directly (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex) -- no redefinition.

result.summary:
Implemented lib/letflow/design/req044-transition-kernel.md exactly: 3 files under lib/letflow/engine/ (Letflow.Engine.Token, Letflow.Engine.InstanceState, Letflow.Engine.Transition). Token/InstanceState are plain structs (design §2/§3), reusing Letflow.Definitions.Graph/Graph.Node from lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex directly -- no redefinition of Graph/Node/Edge/NodeType anywhere under lib/letflow/engine/ (confirmed: only `defstruct`/`defmodule` for InstanceState and Token appear there). Transition module implements transition_event/0, pending_event/0 (term(), per design's deliberate-placeholder rationale), transition_error/0 (5 variants), transition/3's full @spec and body, dispatch_node/4's 5-way (+1 catch-all) dispatch, real bodies for :START (§6.1, advance to first outgoing edge in declaration order), :END (§6.2, remove token, status -> :completed iff tokens now empty), :HUMAN_TASK (§6.3, token stays put, appended to pending_task_nodes), and named-function stubs dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 / dispatch_parallel_gateway/4 each returning {:error, {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, node_type, node_id}} (§6.4/§6.5) plus a generic catch-all for :SERVICE_TASK/:TIMER/:SUB_PROCESS/unknown atoms returning {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, node_type, node_id}} (§6.6). Both verbatim moduledoc sections (§9 Zig std.json.ObjectMap allocator-ownership divergence note, §10 REQ-043 dependency-ordering note) copied byte-for-byte into Letflow.Engine.InstanceState's @moduledoc, per the design's own 'ELIXIR-DEV's placement choice, content is fixed' instruction.

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors` output: 'Compiling 8 files (.ex)\nGenerated letflow app' -- exit 0, zero warnings, first try.

`mix format --check-formatted` output: empty (exit 0) -- files were already correctly formatted as written, no reformat needed.

Self-review (handoff acceptance_criteria):
- `grep -n "Repo\\.|Logger\\.|DateTime\\.|System\\.os_time|System\\.system_time|HTTPoison|Req\\.|File\\.|:rand\\.|:crypto\\." lib/letflow/engine/*.ex` -- only matches are inside the moduledoc's own prose (documenting the purity contract in words) and the copy-pasted verification grep command itself in the moduledoc; zero matches in actual code.
- Determinism: ran `mix run --no-start -e` (no DB/app start needed -- pure module) calling `transition/3` twice with an identical (snapshot, state, event) triple -- `r1 == r2` printed `true`.
- Manually exercised all 5 dispatch cases plus the catch-all plus all 3 error paths via the same `mix run --no-start -e` script: START advances token n1->n2 and leaves pending_task_nodes/status unchanged; HUMAN_TASK leaves token at n2 and appends it to pending_task_nodes; END on a single-token instance removes the token and sets status: :completed; EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY and PARALLEL_GATEWAY return their {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, ...} stub tuples naming the node id; SERVICE_TASK (an unhandled node_type) returns {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :SERVICE_TASK, "n6"}; a bogus event tuple and a non-tuple event both return {:unknown_event_type, ...} naming the offending event value, never raise; an unknown token_id returns {:unknown_token_id, ...}; a token positioned on a node_id absent from the snapshot graph returns {:unknown_node_id, "does-not-exist"}, naming the offending id.
- No second copy of DefinitionGraph/GraphNode/GraphEdge/NodeType anywhere under lib/letflow/engine/ -- verified via `grep -n "defstruct|defmodule" lib/letflow/engine/*.ex`: only Letflow.Engine.InstanceState and Letflow.Engine.Token define structs; Letflow.Engine.Transition defines no struct at all and aliases Letflow.Definitions.Graph / Letflow.Definitions.Graph.Node.
- No existing state-machine's shape changed (process_instance.ex untouched) -- README.md's ASCII state diagram (draft/submitted/approved) does not apply to this new, not-yet-wired-in pure module, so it was left as-is; noted rather than silently skipped.
- `mix test` was not run for this pure-module change since no test file exists yet -- TEST-DESIGNER (a later WF-02 step, after SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER) writes the ExUnit coverage for this module; nothing under test/ was added or touched by this handoff.
